A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EPO study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–F support reliable comparison; relocated material can be matched across versions.

before.justification: V5 reports original evaluations on SOTOPIA, WebShop and ALFWorld, including self-play experiments, component ablations and generated dialogue examples.

after.justification: V6 retains original benchmark experiments and adds baseline results, ablations, training-time measurements and case studies.

M1.justification: The proposed EPO architecture, REINFORCE objective, process-reward construction, inference procedure and iterative self-play remain unchanged in Section 3. V6 tests SFT initialization and an alternative reward model as experimental variants without replacing the proposed RL-only pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions train and evaluate within SOTOPIA/SOTOPIA-π, WebShop and ALFWorld, retaining the hard and unseen-task evaluations. Added examples illustrate existing shopping, household and competitive-dialogue coverage; they do not establish a new task or environment.

E2.justification: V6 substantively revises PPDPP by replacing its RoBERTa planner with Llama3-8B-Instruct. It adds a single-model RL comparator on SOTOPIA in Table 3, alongside the retained direct-SFT comparator. Conversely, v5 Table 6's direct-SFT comparisons on WebShop and ALFWorld disappear. These changes materially revise the comparative evidence for EPO's design.

E3.justification: The PPDPP backbone changes, and new experiments test SFT initialization, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct as PRM, and training times on four A100 GPUs. Existing dataset counts, splits, decoding settings and core hyperparameters remain unchanged. Appendix B also drops product type from the stated WebShop reward factors, without establishing that the scorer changed or results were recomputed.

E4.justification: V6 Table 4 adds tests of whether preliminary SFT is necessary and whether an alternative PRM works. Appendix D adds computational-cost analysis, while Tables 12–14 add shopping and household traces plus a competitive-dialogue failure case. These substantially broaden the diagnostic evidence beyond v5's component ablations, self-play analysis and negotiation example.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly report single-run results because of computational costs: v5 Appendix D and v6 Appendix C. V6 introduces no seed reporting, confidence intervals, repeated-run estimates or significance tests; the expanded tables retain point estimates.

E6.justification: With its revised backbone, PPDPP's GPT-4o Hard/All goal scores change from 6.09/7.94 to 6.65/8.30. Direct-SFT SOTOPIA goals change from 6.65/8.20 to 5.51/7.27 without an explained protocol revision. V6 adds direct-RL results, SFT-initialized EPO scores of 7.26/8.62, Qwen-PRM scores of 7.36/8.67, timings and case outcomes. Direct-SFT WebShop 62.6 and ALFWorld 61.4/60.4 disappear. Retained EPO scores in Tables 1–2 and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and Equations 1–5 are unchanged, with no added theorem, proof or derivation. V6 clarifies that the normalization denominator serves as the stated variance-reduction baseline, but does not change the formula or provide new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about EPO, transferability and benchmark performance persist. V6 adds a concrete conclusion claim that its multi-turn RL has computational costs similar to SFT and emphasizes avoiding preliminary SFT in the introduction's contributions, modestly extending the efficiency framing.

C2.justification: V6 interprets the new ablations as showing little benefit from preliminary SFT and competitive performance with an alternative PRM. Section 4.3 adds the explanation that rigid opponent behavior can undermine strategic flexibility. Conversely, v5 Appendix C's explanation that frozen GPT-4o limits ALFWorld performance, where EPO-SFT trails direct SFT, is removed.

D1.justification: V6 discloses training times, SFT-before-RL initialization, subset use during self-play iterations, and PPDPP's one-agent support. Timing experiments specify four A100 GPUs while the general implementation paragraph still states six. The code/data link changes from the EPO directory in AlibabaResearch/DAMO-ConvAI to lxqpku/EPO. Existing prompts and most hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V6 adds the Qwen2.5 technical report by Yang et al. for the alternative PRM and removes the RoBERTa reference by Liu et al. following the PPDPP backbone revision. The related-work discussion and positioning against planning, prompting and RL approaches otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: V6 makes localized wording, capitalization and affiliation edits, expands experimental discussion, and adds Ethics Statement and Acknowledgments sections. Appendix C's additional-results narrative is removed, implementation details move from D to C, and D becomes Computational Costs. The main narrative structure and prompt text are largely retained.

P2.justification: The comparative displays are substantially revised: v5's cross-domain Table 6 gives way to a main-text SOTOPIA comparison and a new performance/time table; the ablation table expands; and three case tables are added. Dataset-table formatting and several placements change. All four figure graphics themselves are identical, so their relocation does not represent new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: V6 adds useful baseline comparisons, SFT/PRM ablations, timing information and a failure case. However, it removes v5 Appendix C/Table 6's physical-task comparisons and explicit ALFWorld qualification, where direct SFT scored 61.4/60.4 versus EPO-SFT's 45.9/44.1. Direct-SFT SOTOPIA scores also change without explanation. The improved diagnostic evidence and loss of important contrary evidence create a material tradeoff whose net effect on paper quality cannot be reliably determined from the PDFs.
